comparisons.evidence: P's strongest proposal, "risk-triaged human callback," improves outreach to likely absentees; Q's "Elastic Attendance Window" and "Reverse Appointment" remove exact-time compliance or unnecessary physical attendance, addressing larger structural sources of no-shows.

P credibly links targeted callbacks to attendance, but proposals such as "visible social-cost waitlist" and a kiosk assumed to create a "stronger cue" depend on uncertain behavioral effects. Q more directly connects mechanisms to outcomes: protected replacement encourages early slot release, while late-bound windows absorb timing uncertainty.

P's "top-decile" callback pilot and confirmation-copy test are inexpensive, but human calling requires recurring staff capacity and "auto-cancelled unless" check-in risks excluding vulnerable patients. Q's elastic windows require workflow changes, yet its manual "replacement within seven days" exchange pilot is adoptable and aligns patient incentives.

P specifies model inputs, a targeted callback group, and an A/B message test; Q similarly specifies a "three-hour guaranteed window," virtual queue, randomized comparison, and a 30–50-patient manual exchange. Both make their leading mechanisms readily testable.

P offers non-obvious variations such as "boarding-call check-in" and neighborhood pre-check-in, but several remain commitment or outreach interventions. Q introduces deeper reframings—"late-bound service access," transferable appointment rights with protected access, and care beginning before deciding whether attendance is needed.

P spans targeted contact, positive incentives, clinician relationships, physical cues, household coordination, social pressure, and active check-in. Q covers distinct structural levers including timing-risk absorption, checkpointed care, graceful degradation, transferable rights, mobile delivery, third-party permission, cross-branch portability, and eliminating unnecessary visits.

P retains weaker or overlapping items such as a pledge, clinician-identity messaging, a social-cost SMS, and two attendance rewards, and it conflates an actual slot marketplace with mere waitlist visibility. Q more consistently merges by causal pathway and elevates three complementary mechanisms: flexible access, protected exchange, and appointment avoidance.
